citations.quote: fetchFreshPool (src/utils/uniswap.ts): factory.getPool → slot0 + liquidity → nowy Pool z tymi samymi tokenami/fee
fail-open (zwraca stary pool, gdy fabryka/RPC zawiedzie)
wpięty w useRebalanceExecution i useRotateExecution tuż przed buildMintStep
fetchFreshPool poprawny [factory.getPool → slot0+liquidity → nowy Pool, fail-open], wpięty w oba hooki przed buildMintStep

perQuestion.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) refreshes a Uniswap v3 pool's on-chain state before a mint step. It calls factory.getPool to get the pool address, then reads slot0 (current tick/price) and liquidity from the chain, and constructs a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It is fail-open: if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the old pool object instead of throwing. It is wired into useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution immediately before buildMintStep, so the mint amounts are computed from fresh price/liquidity data rather than a stale pool snapshot. A known caveat: the range ticks still come from the original plan (calculated at the old price), so after a price move the range is slightly off-center.
